analysis: The supplied units are head-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (lines 10687-12333). They are public synthetic prompt-contract test vectors: repeated 'summarize' and 'Public synthetic cache-parity input' strings, tool schemas, harmony tool-call messages, token_ids arrays, chain hashes and a prompt_contract_id. I found no secrets, credentials, keys, attestation material, or executable code, and no change to authorization, App Attest (TB-011, A-016), the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), or encryption logic. The file_changes patch excerpt is truncated (patch_excerpt_complete=false). It shows fixture updates: an additional_context.enable_thinking=false field, changed prompt_token_count values, and changed chain hashes. Those changes relate to the prefix-cache/prompt-contract determinism area (T-041), and the cache keys derive from the plan/chain hashes. The consuming code is not supplied, so I cannot verify that the new vectors match the Swift/Go implementation. Open integration questions: whether the updated vectors correctly mirror the production prompt builder, and whether the cache-isolation properties in T-041 are unaffected by the contract change. Those would be covered by the tests that consume the fixtures, which are outside the supplied evidence. No security regression is identifiable from the fixture data alone.
